summary.headline: Parag Milk Foods Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR1,241 crore, up 23% YoY, with volumes up 12% and EBITDA up 37% excluding last year's one-off.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue reached a record INR1,241 crore, with about half the growth from volume (12%) and the rest from price and mix. Gross profit rose 24% to INR323 crore and gross margin was 26% versus 25.8% a year ago, with gross margin per litre up from INR14 to INR17 despite milk costs rising about INR7 per litre. EBITDA excluding last year's FX MTM one-off was INR101 crore (8.1% margin, up 37%), and PAT grew 42% to INR42 crore. Net debt rose to INR678 crore from INR484 crore in March 2026, driven by inventory build-up from inflation and festive stocking, and management expects debt to stay in a similar range.

segments.name: Flagship categories (ghee, cheese, paneer, curd)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR778 crore in Q2, up 20% in value and 7% in volume. Paneer had its strongest volume quarter; ghee grew double digits in volume; Gowardhan holds 22% share in branded cow ghee.

segments.name: New Age (Pride of Cows, Avvatar)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR154 crore, up 71% YoY and 12% of revenue. Avvatar reports about 15% online whey protein share and over 75% of its revenue from quick commerce, e-commerce and its own website.

segments.name: Ingredients (MPC, lactose)
segments.commentary: Management said this segment grew exceptionally well in Q2, led by milk protein concentrate and lactose. No figures were given.

segments.name: Regions
segments.commentary: All four regions grew at high double digits; South and West were the fastest-growing. Regional disclosure was added this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects high single-digit volume growth in core categories (paneer, ghee) in coming quarters, with no price increase planned in core categories.
Milk prices are not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought and deficient rains; procurement is at about INR46.5/litre and may hold through Q3.
Blended gross margin of 26-27% is expected to continue, with no dilution from new capacity.
A&P spend is expected to stay in the INR130-150 crore annual range; ~INR20 crore of Q2 spend is treated as non-recurring.
Net debt is not expected to fall materially; it may rise marginally as capex is funded. Management expects positive operating cash flow for FY27 as inventory unwinds.
New Age business targets a ~25% revenue share on the way to the INR10,000 crore ambition; management declined to give FY27 or FY28 growth numbers.
capex_capacity: Paneer: capacity rising 4x from 20 to 80 metric tons per day across Manchar and Palamaner, about INR100 crore, commissioning by June 2027; management expects about 80% utilisation soon after commissioning.

Cheese: capacity doubling from 60 to 120 metric tons per day for about INR105 crore at existing sites, phased 80, 100, then 120, with completion targeted for Q2 FY28; whey protein output doubles with it.
Combined capex of INR205 crore approved; management separately described a capex outlay of over INR200 crore for the year.
Board approved amalgamation of wholly owned subsidiary Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms into the company, subject to approvals.
Capex has been funded from internal accruals over the past three years; ECLGS 5.0 working capital funding and a new consortium lender were added this year.
demand_pricing: Two price increases were taken in the quarter; no further core-category price increase is planned.
Organised paneer share is low: management estimates 70-80% of out-of-home paneer is analogue, and about 4 million kg/day of paneer is consumed in India.
B2C grew double digits in Q2 and B2B was deliberately limited, as in Q1; overall mix is about 70% B2C and 30% B2B.
Management sees no price war from Milky Mist's capacity expansion (100 to 350 for paneer/cheese); it cites brand strength and distribution as its edge.
Management said blended gross margin is 26-27% and that cheese and whey are assessed together; no product-level margins are disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 7% flagship volume growth came from B2C festive stocking versus institutional buying, and how much of the INR177 crore other expenses is non-recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C grew double digits in both Q2 and last year's Q2, and B2B was consciously limited. About INR20 crore of Q2 spend is one-off brand building; the rest is variable cost (power, fuel, supply chain) and A&P within an annual budget.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view New Age growth and margins going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: New Age revenue reached INR154 crore in Q2 (INR118 crore in Q1, INR100 crore in Q4 FY26), an ARR above INR600 crore. Management did not give FY28 growth numbers but targets about 25% New Age share at the INR10,000 crore milestone.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for milk procurement cost in Q3 and Q4, given South cooperative price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Milk is at INR46.5/litre and is not expected to soften in Q3 because of drought. Karnataka's KMF raised prices, and some South response is possible; the South is 20-25% of procurement.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory and net debt high, and will cash flow turn positive by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the rise mainly to inflation and festive inventory; inventory days are stable. It expects the inventory build to unwind by year-end and believes FY27 operating cash flow will be positive.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement, and how will the new cheese and whey capacity affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin per litre rose from INR14 to INR17 despite milk up INR7/litre; ingredients (MPC, lactose) grew strongly. Management says blended margin of 26-27% will hold as cheese and whey capacity doubles.

qa_highlights.question: What is the paneer and cheese capacity ramp, and what utilisation to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Paneer reaches 80 MT/day by June 2027 and could be about 80% utilised right away (roughly INR500-600 crore incremental revenue was suggested by an analyst). Cheese phases from 60 to 80 MT next month or so, then 100 and 120 MT by Q2 FY28; management assumes 80% utilisation.

risks_watch: Working capital and net debt (INR678 crore) are elevated; the company says FY27 operating cash flow should turn positive as inventory unwinds, which needs to be tracked.
Milk cost inflation: procurement at INR46.5/litre with no seasonal softening expected in Q3 because of drought; South cooperative price hikes could add pressure.
Other expenses rose to INR177 crore, including ~INR20 crore of brand spend that management calls non-recurring; A&P discipline is to be checked.
Capacity additions (paneer June 2027, cheese Q2 FY28) depend on demand absorption; new competitors such as Milky Mist are expanding paneer and cheese capacity.
Gross margin guidance of 26-27% is blended, and the company does not disclose product-level margins, which limits visibility into New Age and cheese economics.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the capacity plan, with specific numbers. Cautious on the balance sheet: management was less clear on debt and cash-flow timing and declined to give FY27 or FY28 growth numbers.
key_quotes: Volumes grew by 12% this quarter, which accounts to about half of the increase and the remainder came from pricing and product mix.
We are increasingly seeing product availability and capacity determining the pace at which we can serve the market.
So I don't see any price war and all this things. It's only the ability to sell the brand, which we have and the distribution is very important.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin per litre rose from INR14 to INR17 and gross margin is 26% vs 25.8%, but management guides only a flat 26-27% blended range while milk costs stay high.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Paneer capacity goes 4x from 20 to 80 MT/day by June 2027 (~INR100 crore) and cheese doubles from 60 to 120 MT/day by Q2 FY28 (~INR105 crore), both under construction with dates.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides high single-digit core-category volume growth, with Q2 volume up 12% and H1 up 8%, and the new paneer and cheese capacity comes online through 2027.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board already approved INR205 crore for paneer and cheese and management guided a capex outlay of over INR200 crore for the year, so the capex cycle is active, though no new capex beyond this was flagged.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is held at high single-digit core volume growth and 26-27% blended gross margin, with no core-category price increase planned, so there is no clear reason to raise it.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Milk procurement at INR46.5/litre (up from INR38, +18% YoY) is not expected to soften in Q3 due to drought, and South cooperative price hikes could add pressure; net debt rose to INR678 crore from INR484 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New Age revenue reached INR154 crore in Q2 (+71% YoY, 12% of revenue) and the company targets about 25% New Age share, but no specific new product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Inventory unwind and positive FY27 operating cash flow
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR678 crore from INR484 crore and H1 operating cash use was INR84 crore; management expects inventory to unwind and FY27 operating cash flow to be positive, but this is not yet evidenced.

rows.label: New Age business scale-up toward 25% revenue share
rows.why: New Age revenue grew from INR100 crore in Q4 FY26 to INR118 crore in Q1 and INR154 crore in Q2 FY27, and Avvatar has over 75% of revenue from quick commerce and online channels.

rows.label: Amalgamation of Bhagyalaxmi Dairy Farms
rows.why: Board approved the amalgamation of the wholly owned subsidiary into the company, subject to approvals, but no timing or financial impact was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing discipline and the paneer and cheese capacity plan, but cautious on the balance sheet, with less clarity on debt and cash-flow timing and no FY27 or FY28 growth numbers. Analysts pushed on milk cost and South cooperative price hikes, inventory and net debt
